headline: South Korea's Literature Translation Institute says 21 works by Korean writers, including Han Kang and Hwang Sok-yong, appear on the list of books eligible for payment in Anthropic's $1.5 billion copyright settlement.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: specific, attributed finding by a Korean literary body, but it concerns eligibility under an existing US settlement, not a new ruling.
importance_line: Korean authors and publishers may be able to claim about $3,000 per work, and the case adds pressure on AI firms to disclose which books they train on, but the list shows works eligible under a US settlement, not a Korean ruling, and authors must file a claim to be paid.
summary: Chosunbiz reports that Anthropic appears to have used works by Korean writers without permission, after the Literature Translation Institute of Korea (LTI Korea) said on 17 Oct 2026 that it found 21 such works on the claims list of Anthropic's settlement of a US class action over books allegedly downloaded illegally to train its AI, and notified the authors. About 500,000 titles qualify for roughly $3,000 per work if the authors take part in the claims process, an LTI Korea official said the institute will support legal action if needed, and the Korean Publishers Association has called for AI companies to disclose which copyrighted works they use and to pay fairly.
notes: Chosunbiz says the settlement was agreed 'in July this year'; the Anthropic settlement is widely reported to have been announced in September 2025, so the entry leaves the month out and the main session may want to check. The article hedges ('appear to have used'); the entry keeps the hedge and does not say a court found misuse.
